title: Wringer gate concurrency record
description: `concurrency.json` — which gates ran BESIDE which in one `wring verify`. A SIBLING of manifest.json, like vacuity.json, acceptance.json and stability.json, and for the same law-7 reason: `wringer.evidence.v1` is frozen and `gate-result.schema.json` is closed, so the mark cannot go on the row it describes. ABSENT when every gate ran alone, which is every bundle written before this existed and every repo that has not declared `concurrent: true` on anything. **It exists because duration_ms is not private to a run.** `wring health` compares it across a window and flags drift past 2x, so a contended wall clock — a real measurement of a different quantity — must be excluded from that comparison rather than reported as the gate slowing. Health reads this file, excludes those rows from the duration trend, and COUNTS the exclusion, because a ratio over four of twelve runs is a different claim from one over twelve. Nothing here decides a verdict: concurrency changes a duration and never a pass/fail, which is why SPEC_ACCEPT §3 clause 2 survives it untouched.

gates.description: One row per gate that ran beside another, in declared order. Never empty: a run with no concurrent group writes no file at all, so a reader never has to tell an empty record from a missing one.

group.description: Which group this gate ran in, 1-based over the groups of the whole run. Groups are maximal runs of CONSECUTIVE `concurrent: true` gates and execute in declared order, so a reader can reconstruct the schedule from this number alone.

beside.description: The other gates in the same group, by id. Present because "this gate was concurrent" is not actionable on its own: a reader looking at an inflated duration wants to know what it was competing with.
